protocol:
1. Keep labeled reagent/sample microcentrifuge tubes chilled in an ice bucket and set thin-walled PCR tubes in tube racks on the bench.

2. Assemble each PCR reaction on ice by pipetting aliquots from the chilled tubes into thin-walled PCR tubes using a single-channel micropipette and disposable tips; prepare 20 µL total reaction volume per tube.

3. Cap each PCR tube securely after the reaction components are added.

4. Briefly spin down the capped PCR tubes in a benchtop mini-centrifuge with the blue rotor to collect liquid at the bottom of the tubes.

5. Place the spun-down PCR tubes into the Bio-Rad T100 thermal cycler block and close the heated lid.

6. Run the saved T100 thermal cycler program named “PHANTA” with 20 µL reaction volume: 95°C for 30 s; 33 cycles of 95°C for 10 s, 67°C for 6 s, and 72°C for 6 s; 72°C for 1 min; then hold at 12°C, with the lid set to 77°C.
